    Instructor Notes

    Overall approach

    • This module is for complete beginners. Each Python notebook takes 15 to 25 minutes and covers one idea, with an exercise and its solution at the end. In a live session, teach the episode page briefly, then let learners work through the notebooks while helpers circulate.
    • Suggested timing for a full day: Introduction 30 min; Python Basics (notebooks 2a to 2f) 2.5 hours; Working with Data (3a, 3b) 1 hour; Geospatial Python Basics (4a to 4d) 2 hours; Map Your County in Python 1 hour. The QGIS episodes (Getting Started 1.75 hours, Tables 1.25 hours, Map Your County 1 hour) work well as a separate day.
    • Ask everyone to Save a copy in Drive before running anything.
    • The examples use Indiana counties and Lafayette food stores throughout, so the same data reappears in later modules (Data Collection, Case Studies).
    • The Python notebooks were rewritten for beginners from the Workshop 2026 Session B notebook (intro_python.ipynb), which stays in its own repository unchanged.

    Episode by episode

    Introduction

    • The “Which tool?” challenge is a good opener: there is no single right answer for the visual check.

    Python Basics

    • Normalize errors early: run the deliberate SyntaxError and NameError cells in notebook 2a together and read the last line aloud.
    • The “numbers stored as text” idea (2b) comes back in every Census notebook and in the join notebook (4c).

    Working with Data

    • Point out that describe() averages the FIPS codes (3a). It is a memorable way to show why identifiers should be text.
    • The log scale in the scatter plot (3b) is often new; show the same chart without it first.

    Geospatial Python Basics

    • The wrong-CRS demonstration in 4b (Indiana ends up near the equator) makes the difference between set_crs() and to_crs() stick.
    • In 4c, the failing join is deliberate. Let learners read the error before showing the fix.
    • 58 of the 64 food stores lie inside the city limits; all 17 supermarkets do.
    • 4d: the commonest mistake is reading without masked=True and reporting -9999 as the lowest elevation. Elevation 152.9 to 258.1 m; cultivated crops cover 65% of the county.

    Map Your County (Python and QGIS)

    • Both capstones use the same files and should produce the same map; pair a Python learner with a QGIS learner and compare at the end.
    • Expected: 43 tracts, 0 unmatched; tract 104 (residence halls) has 0 households and a poverty universe of 0, so its rates are missing; median income is -666666666 for tracts 104 and 105; 17 tracts have 10% or more households without a vehicle. Natural breaks differ slightly between tools: about 4, 9, 15 and 26% in Python (mapclassify) and 2.4, 8.6, 15.3 and 25.5% in QGIS. Both are fine; it is a nice point about methods.
    • QGIS does not draw features whose Graduated value is NULL. The hint shows a rule-based “no data” class.
    • Discuss the poverty map near campus: student populations raise poverty rates. It is a good moment to talk about what a Census measure does and does not mean.

    Getting Started with QGIS

    • Moved here from the Data Visualization module in October 2026 and rebuilt in Step 8 on Indiana colleges (the Alaska airports remain in Workshop Session 1A). Data is loaded from this repository’s data/ folder by URL. Each part ends with a Check line; ask learners to confirm it before moving on.
    • QGIS 4: in Add Vector Layer > Protocol, the Type list starts with cloud services (Alibaba Cloud OSS is preselected). Learners must pick HTTP/HTTPS/FTP, or the layer fails to load. QGIS 3 preselects HTTP.
    • The OpenStreetMap basemap needs an internet connection; on a slow network, skip it.
    • Loading from a web address (Layer > Add Layer > Add Vector Layer > Protocol: HTTP(S)) avoids file downloads and path problems. If a network blocks it, the same GeoJSON files can be downloaded from the repository’s data/ folder and loaded as files.
    • In QGIS, the OpenStreetMap basemap works normally. (In Colab it does not, which is why the notebooks use an Esri basemap.)
    • Learners often press OK instead of Apply while comparing classification modes; encourage Apply so the dialog stays open.
    • Remind learners to rename layers before making a legend.

    Tables, Joins and Selections in QGIS

    • The ACS CSV loads with correct types because of tippecanoe_acs_2024.csvt. Without it, loading from the web gives text fields, and Delimited Text guesses GEOID as a number.
    • Layers read from the web are read-only, so the Field Calculator only offers virtual fields (ticked and grayed out, with types Decimal (double) and Integer (32 bit)). That is expected.
    • Division by zero returns NULL in QGIS expressions (tract 104). Stress that NULL is not 0%.

    Common problems

    Symptom Likely cause Fix
    NameError A cell was skipped Runtime > Run before
    Colab forgot variables The session disconnected Reconnect and run all cells from the top
    HTTPError or timeout when reading data Network hiccup Rerun the cell
    A merge fails with “object and int64 columns” ID types differ Convert both with .astype(str).str.zfill(5)
    QGIS layer shows nothing Off screen, or behind the basemap Right-click > Zoom to Layer; drag the layer above the basemap
